entry.title: Spin supersolid in triangular lattice easy-axis spin-1/2 antiferromagnet: a fermionic parton perspective
entry.summary:
We study the supersolid order of the spin-1/2 easy-axis XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice using a fermionic parton mean-field theory built on the $π$-flux Dirac spin liquid, with the mean-field order generated by an on-site spinon interaction term and nearest-neighbor (anisotropic) spin couplings. The collective modes are obtained using the random-phase approximation (RPA). In a finite parameter region, we find the Y state as a self-consistent solution, together with the competing Y' state, which is a $90^\circ$-rotated Y state inside the order plane.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #post-quantum

entry.title: Zirah: A Post-Quantum True Random Number Generator Hardware Signer With an Avalanche Noise
entry.summary:
Zirah is a hardware signer built around an STM32F407 microcontroller, and its purpose is to find out, on inexpensive hardware, where a post-quantum signing key is exposed and what actually protects it. The device draws every random bit from a reverse-biased 2N3904 junction in avalanche breakdown, amplified by an LM358 and screened by SP 800-90B health tests, computes ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204, hedged) on the STM32 with two-share arithmetic masking of the secret-key multiplications, and adds ECDSA P-256 from an ATECC608 secure element over the same digest, once a person has matched an eight-digit digest prefix on its OLED with the PC and pressed a button. A desktop application and a command-line tool drive the board and verify its output, and because only a 32-byte manifest digest reaches the device, it signs files of any type and size, returning signed copies for PDF, Office Open XML, ZIP, PNG and JPEG files and detached records for every other format.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #post-quantum

entry.title: Generalized Batched Decomposition Key-Switching for CKKS. In lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes, ciphertexts carry an inherent noise that grows as computation advances.
entry.summary:
In lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes, ciphertexts carry an inherent noise that grows as computation advances. The key-switching procedure of these schemes allows the homomorphic re-encryption of a ciphertext under a new secret key, but it incurs substantial noise growth and computational cost. In this work, we generalize the RNS-based decomposition technique of the CKKS scheme to an arbitrary number of input polynomials and secret keys.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #neuroscience

entry.title: Atlantis: Lattice-based Anonymous Tokens with Private Metadata Bit. Anonymous tokens with private metadata bit (ATPM) allow an issuer to embed a hidden trust flag, as a single bit, within issued tokens.
entry.summary:
Anonymous tokens with private metadata bit (ATPM) allow an issuer to embed a hidden trust flag, as a single bit, within issued tokens. The bit remains hidden from the clients, but verifiers can read the bit and rate-limit or discard tokens marked suspect. A series of ATPM constructions exist in the literature, however all current constructions rely on classical hardness assumptions such as RSA groups, pairings, or elliptic-curve VRFs and do not provide any post-quantum security guarantees.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #post-quantum
